groups.title: Tablet (E14800ATB)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used to supply vitamins E, B1, B2, B6 and C in physical tiredness, in pregnancy and breast-feeding, when strength is reduced during or after an illness and in later life; for beriberi, tired eyes, neuralgia, muscle pain and joint pain (back pain, stiff shoulders and the like); for angular cheilitis, cheilitis, stomatitis, glossitis, eczema and dermatitis; and to supply zinc.
groups.usage: Those aged 8 years and over and adults: take 1 tablet, 1 time in 1 day.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a baby under 12 months of age, if you have severe kidney failure, or if you have a hereditary problem such as galactose intolerance, Lapp lactase deficiency or glucose-galactose malabsorption. Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if the user is a premature baby or an infant; if you have high oxalate levels in the urine; if you have a gastrointestinal disease such as peptic ulcer, chronic ulcerative colitis or regional colitis; if you have impaired heart or circulatory function, kidney disorder, a low protein level in the blood, gout or kidney stones; if you have a tendency to thrombosis; or if you are short of folic acid. Keep to the stated dosage and schedule. When it is given to a child, give it under the guidance and supervision of a guardian. It can interfere with the detection of sugar in urine tests and can turn the urine yellow, so it may affect laboratory test results. If there is no improvement in symptoms after about 1 month of use, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

Do not take it together with phosphates, calcium salts, oral tetracycline preparations, antacids or levodopa. Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with an oral contraceptive containing oestrogen, anti-aldosterone medicines or triamterene. Avoid tea containing tannin, such as green tea and black tea, during the period of use and just before and after a dose.

If nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, loose stools, constipation, stomach discomfort, gastrointestinal disturbance, digestive disturbance, upper abdominal pain, rash, reddening, red patches, cardiac arrest (stopping of the heartbeat), reduced function of the central nervous system, dermatitis, an unpleasant smell of sweat or breath, hair loss, impatience, low blood pressure or fluid in the lungs occurs, or if a period comes earlier than expected, the bleeding gradually becomes heavier, or bleeding lasts a long time, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

summaryTable.What it is for: Supply of vitamins E, B1, B2, B6 and C and of zinc, with relief of beriberi, tired eyes, nerve, muscle and joint pain, and mouth and skin inflammation

groups.title: Eye drops (228742COS)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the temporary relief of swelling of the cornea (corneal oedema).
groups.usage: Instil 1 to 2 drops into the affected eye every 3 to 4 hours.
groups.caution:
Before using this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have hypersensitivity to propylene glycol or have had it. To avoid contaminating this medicine, do not let the tip of the container touch any outside surface. Do not use it if its colour has changed or if it has become cloudy.

If pain in the eye, a change in sight, continuing redness or a feeling of irritation occurs, stop using it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist. A temporary burning feeling and irritation may occur.

groups.title: Syrup (471300ASY)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the temporary relief of itchy eyes, watering eyes, runny nose, itching of the nose or the throat, sneezing, blocked nose and congestion of the sinuses.
groups.usage: Adults and those aged 12 years and over: take 4 teaspoons (20 mL) at a time. Those aged 6 years and over but under 12 years: take 2 teaspoons (10 mL) at a time. Those aged 2 years and over but under 6 years: take 1 teaspoon (5 mL) at a time. Take it every 4 to 6 hours, and not more than 4 times in 24 hours.
groups.caution:
If a severe skin reaction such as acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis occurs, stop taking it and consult a doctor or pharmacist.

People with severe or uncontrolled high blood pressure must not take this medicine.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if the user is an infant under 2 years of age, or if you have heart disease, high blood pressure, thyroid disease, diabetes, glaucoma, or a breathing disorder such as asthma or chronic bronchitis.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.

Do not take it together with monoamine oxidase inhibitors (MAOIs — some medicines for depression, mental and emotional disorders and Parkinson's disease).
Do not take this medicine if you stopped taking a monoamine oxidase inhibitor (some medicines for depression, mental and emotional disorders and Parkinson's disease) within the last 2 weeks.
Consult a doctor or pharmacist if you take it together with sedatives or tranquillisers.

If anxiety, dizziness or insomnia occurs, if a sore throat lasts for 2 days or more, or if headache, fever, rash, nausea, vomiting, acute generalised exanthematous pustulosis (AGEP), erythema, many small pustules or ischaemic colitis (sudden abdominal pain, rectal bleeding and the like) occurs, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
If symptoms of reversible posterior encephalopathy syndrome or reversible cerebral vasoconstriction syndrome (a sudden severe headache, thunderclap headache, nausea, vomiting, confusion, seizures, visual disturbance and the like) occur, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Excitement (especially in children) and drowsiness may occur.

groups.title: Capsule (D39400ACH)
groups.efficacy: This is an over-the-counter medicine used for the relief of blocked nose, runny nose, sneezing, watering eyes, sore throat and a heavy feeling in the head caused by a nasal cold (acute rhinitis), allergic rhinitis or sinusitis.
groups.usage: Adults: take 1 capsule at a time, 3 times in 1 day, after meals.
groups.caution:
Do not take this medicine if you have hypersensitivity to it, if the user is a child under 2 years of age, or if you are taking an MAO inhibitor (antidepressant, antipsychotic, mood stabiliser, anti-Parkinson medicine and the like) or stopped taking one within the last 2 weeks.
Before taking this medicine, consult a doctor or pharmacist if you have an allergic constitution or have had allergic symptoms caused by a medicine (for example fever, rash, joint pain, asthma, itching); if you have high blood pressure, heart disease, glaucoma (eye pain, blurred vision), difficulty passing urine, thyroid disease or diabetes; if you are physically weak or have a high fever; if you are pregnant, may be pregnant or are breast-feeding; if you are an older person; if you smoke, or have asthma, chronic bronchitis, emphysema, a cough with a lot of phlegm, a cough lasting or coming back for more than 1 week, a chronic cough, or a cough with fever, rash or a persistent headache; or if you have hypersensitivity to Food Yellow No. 5 or have had an allergic reaction to it.
If there is no improvement in symptoms after 5 or 6 doses, stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
Keep to the stated dosage and schedule.
Drowsiness may occur after a dose, so be careful when driving or operating machinery.

Do not take it together with other oral medicines for rhinitis or with oral medicines containing antihistamines (cold medicines, cough and expectorant medicines, travel sickness medicines, allergy medicines).
Do not drink alcohol while you are taking it.

If haemorrhagic stroke, nausea, vomiting, persistent or severe thirst, constipation, loss of appetite, rash, reddening, itching, difficulty passing urine, headache, facial flushing or unusual sensitivity to light occurs, or rarely shock (hives, swelling and tightness of the chest immediately after a dose, together with pallor, cold hands and feet, cold sweat and difficulty breathing), stop taking it immediately and consult a doctor or pharmacist.
